implementation: All server semantic graph loads use the installed compiler package graph, retaining package-local versions and aliases
Completion probes and proposed rename rechecks share the same graph-loading callback as ordinary diagnostics and navigation
Reachable installed sources retain owner identity when opened for semantic browsing through the application entry graph
Installed source buffers must match disk; formatting and completion edits in caches are suppressed; installed declarations and source edits are excluded from rename
Workspace discovery excludes .kalandra; open workspace overlays replace source before parsing
Configured managed manifests must match their startup contents; each graph load revalidates the public lock and snapshot integrity with no Git/installer calls

cases: Application float32 library and a transitive int64 version of the same library remain separate in diagnostics and navigation
Private library import definition and hover navigate to the private installed version rather than application mapping
Unsaved valid root overrides invalid saved source; typed errors appear and clear after buffer edits
References include an eligible unopened workspace caller and original installed declaration
Workspace binding and explicit import alias rename succeeds; installed declaration rename and prepareRename reject edits
Workspace scope completion uses installed imports; cached source formatting produces no edits
Changed installed buffer prevents analysis; closing restores disk source
Missing/corrupt lock, corrupted snapshot and changed startup manifest return no stale semantic information; restoring valid state recovers
Application and cache are relocated after installation; original Git repositories are removed before editor analysis
All application/cache/lock bytes remain unchanged after requests
Relocated installed editor-tools archive repeats the existing framed LSP suite and new package fixture from an unrelated cwd
notes: Initial regression run found old sanitizer executables referencing removed LLVM 22 ASan dylibs. Rebuilding the affected test targets against LLVM 23 corrected these environmental failures.
The old managed-project startup rejection assertion was replaced by positive scoped package protocol qualification.

limits: Synchronous bounded graph checking; no filesystem watching, background indexing, automatic installs or config reload
Installed library browsing is limited to sources reachable through the application entry graph; cached sources cannot be edited through semantic operations
The package fixture enables placement diagnostics but does not execute GPU code or qualify new shader features
No additional operating system, real editor host, remote transport or installed Metal execution is qualified here; third-party LLVM is not sanitizer instrumented
Broader installed Metal onboarding remains in N3-D; authenticated/SSH transport and package update conveniences remain follow-ups
